target_theorem_claims.claim: For a coherent algebraic sheaf on a complex projective variety, every cohomology comparison map H^q(X,F) to H^q(X^an,F^an) is bijective.
Analytification induces a bijection from algebraic homomorphisms F to G to analytic homomorphisms F^an to G^an for coherent algebraic sheaves on a complex projective variety.
Every coherent analytic sheaf on the analytification of a complex projective variety is the analytification of a coherent algebraic sheaf, unique up to isomorphism.

architecture_checks.theorem_1_descending_induction: For B=L, C=F, D=H^{q+1}(R), E=H^{q+1}(L), the surjective half of the four lemma proves epsilon_F^q surjective. Applying that result to R supplies epsilon_R^q surjective; the injective half of the four lemma then proves epsilon_F^q injective.
architecture_checks.theorem_3_no_circularity: At dimension r, Lemma 7 and the algebraization of B in Lemma 8 use essential surjectivity only on the hyperplane of dimension r-1. Theorem 1 and Theorem 2 are already complete before the induction starts.
architecture_checks.lemma_8_stabilization: H^2(C(n))=0 and H^1(B(n))=0 give dim H^1(M(n-1)) >= dim H^1(L_n) >= dim H^1(M(n)); finite-dimensionality makes the integer sequence eventually constant, so H^1(L_n)->H^1(M(n)) is an isomorphism and H^0(M(n))->H^0(B(n)) is surjective.
architecture_checks.lemma_8_nakayama: At x on E, B(n)_x=M/(t)M. Lifted global sections generate this quotient, hence M=N+(t)M=N+mM; M is finite and Nakayama gives M=N.
architecture_checks.completion: Two finite global-generation surjections produce L_1^an -> L_0^an -> M -> 0. Full faithfulness algebraizes the first map and exactness of analytification identifies the cokernel with M.
